sections.h2: Where does my Camillus house sit: town or village?
sections.html:
Camillus is a town in Onondaga County, west of Syracuse, and the first thing to settle is whether your house sits in the town alone or inside the village of Camillus, which lies in the southwestern part of the town. Village residents answer to two sets of local rules and tax bills, and that changes who you call at closing.

A Camillus owner can hire an agent, go it alone, or sell directly to a company such as ours. About four in five households here own their home, so most sellers are individual homeowners.

sections.h2: What do Camillus housing and income figures look like?
sections.html:
Camillus had an estimated 25,088 people in mid-2025, 1.0% fewer than at the April 2020 base. Turnover is low: 92.2% of residents were in the same house a year before.

A $209,000 median home value alongside $85,915 in household income describes a middle-income suburb. More than one in five residents is 65 or older, so some sellers are settling an estate or leaving a larger house.

sections.h2: How big is Camillus and how did it begin?
sections.html:
Camillus spans 34.36 square miles of land, with roughly 738 people to each square mile. Most of the present town belonged to the former Central New York Military Tract, and the first pioneer settler arrived around 1795 at the site of what became the village. Camillus was formed in 1799 from land that had belonged to the Town of Marcellus. The Fairmount area in the southeast was once part of the Onondaga Reservation territory and was annexed to Camillus in 1834.

The Erie Canal arrived in 1825 and spurred industry, and a rail line linking Syracuse to Auburn followed in 1838. Two local landmarks, the Nine Mile Creek Aqueduct and the Wilcox Octagon House, carry National Register listings. Population grew from 6,735 in 1950 to 18,328 in 1960 and 26,841 in 1970, so a large part of the housing is mid-century or newer. A buyer of an older house will ask about the roof, the furnace and the wiring.

sections.h2: Which hamlets, neighborhoods and roads are in Camillus?
sections.html:
Camillus is a mix of hamlets and subdivisions with no single downtown. Wikipedia lists a long run of named places, and a few anchor the housing market.

  • Hamlets: Amboy, Bennetts Corners, Fairmount, Newport, Warners, Memphis and North Belle Isle
  • Neighborhoods near the village: Fox Chapel, Weatheridge, Pioneer Farms, Westview Manor and West Genesee Terrace
  • Southern edge: Scenic Hills, Parson Farms, Stanley Manor and Sherwood Knolls

NY 5 crosses the town from east to west. NY 173 meets it near Fairmount, NY 174 near the village, and NY 321 at Bennetts Corners, while NY 695 and NY 297 run near the east town line. The town also reaches ZIP codes for Camillus (13031), Elbridge, Marcellus, Memphis, Warners and parts of Syracuse, so your mailing address may not say Camillus even when the parcel is in the town. Check the deed and tax bill rather than the postal city.

sections.h2: What is the Camillus economy like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Camillus sits on the west side of Syracuse. Workers spend 21.3 minutes getting to their jobs on average, and 2022 retail sales reached about $719.6 million, or $28,576 per resident. Health care and social assistance receipts for 2022 came to about $91.3 million.

Schooling levels run high in town, with 94.8% of adults finished with high school and 44.6% holding a four-year degree or beyond. The town has about 10,968 households averaging 2.29 people, and the Census Bureau counts 1,152 veterans among residents. Broadband subscriptions reach 92.3% of households and 6.1% of residents were born abroad. A small general aviation airstrip, Camillus Airport, sits near the northern town line, and the former Syracuse Municipal Airport lay in the northeast part of town.

In practical terms, a move-in-ready house competes well against finished homes on the market, while a house with dated kitchens or deferred maintenance does not. A direct buyer prices the work into the offer and skips that comparison.

sections.h2: How is a Camillus deed recorded in Onondaga County?
sections.html:
Every deed in the county goes through the Onondaga County Clerk, and the posted fee schedule lists these costs.

  • $45.50 base fee for a deed, plus $5.00 for each page and $0.50 for each additional surname or cross reference
  • $5.00 to file the TP-584 return, plus $2.00 of state transfer tax for each $500 of price
  • $125.00 for the RP-5217 real property transfer report on an improved residential property
  • $10.00 residential deed note to grantors, required by state law since March 2020

At $210,000, the state transfer tax comes to $840. County land records start in 1794, so ownership can be traced back a long way. The deed department answers recording questions at 315-435-8250.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Onondaga County taxes when I sell?
sections.html:
For parcels outside the city of Syracuse, Camillus among them, bills are handled by the county's tax services office on the 15th floor of the Civic Center on Montgomery Street. Owners can look up bills, print receipts and pay online.

The office states two payment dates for delinquent accounts. County taxes unpaid after March 31 and school or village taxes unpaid after November 1 go to that office, which takes calls at 315-435-2426 and accepts mailed checks payable to the Chief Fiscal Officer at PO Box 1004, Syracuse, NY 13201. The county also holds a yearly online tax auction in October, with properties listed from September.

Anyone who is behind should get a payoff figure before accepting an offer. County exemption applications for parcels outside Syracuse are due March 1, so a seller listing in the winter months should ask the town assessor about the filing.

sections.h2: What should I check with the town before I sell?
sections.html:
Before you list, ask the Town of Camillus code enforcement staff whether any permit on your house was left open, whether a rental on the property needs registration or inspection, and which zoning district applies. An unfinished deck, a finished basement without a permit or an old shed can all surface when a buyer's attorney orders a search.

If the property is in the village of Camillus, ask the village clerk separately for any village charges. The county notes that village taxes have their own November 1 cutoff, so a closing attorney will want both bills.

faqs.q: Is Camillus a town or a village?
faqs.a: Both exist. The Town of Camillus lies west of Syracuse in Onondaga County, and the village of Camillus occupies the southwestern part of it. Your tax bill shows which one levies on your house, and the village clerk can answer questions about village charges.

faqs.q: What is the state transfer tax on a Camillus sale?
faqs.a: Onondaga County's clerk posts it at $2.00 per $500 of price, which makes $840 on a $210,000 sale. It is reported on the TP-584 return, a $5.00 filing.

faqs.q: Which office records my deed after I sell in Camillus?
faqs.a: The Onondaga County Clerk. Recording starts at $45.50 plus $5.00 a page, and the RP-5217 report adds $125.00 on improved residential property.

faqs.q: Can unpaid taxes put a Camillus house in an auction?
faqs.a: They can. The county holds an online tax auction every October, and delinquent taxes outside Syracuse are paid at its tax services office. Clearing the balance first keeps the debt from coming out of your proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Why does my Camillus house have a Syracuse or Marcellus mailing address?
faqs.a: The town spans several postal areas, including 13031 for Camillus plus Elbridge, Marcellus, Memphis, Warners and Syracuse ZIP codes. The deed and the assessment roll show the legal location.
